meta.title: An oral history is one person’s account
meta.summary: A named interview preserves experience without standing for a whole community.

sourceRefs.label: Ohio History Connection · GOHI Oral Histories

blocks.text: Ohio Memory describes oral history as a way to preserve individual experience and to document communities as they change. The Ohio History Connection’s Gay Ohio History Initiative offers a concrete example: its project pages identify narrators and make selected recordings or transcripts available under stated access conditions. Read a testimony as the account of the person named. Its setting matters: who asked the questions, when the interview happened, how the transcript was produced, and what the narrator agreed could be shared. One person’s words can illuminate a life, organization, or moment; they cannot establish what every person in a community believes. When quoting or linking an interview, retain the narrator’s name, collection title, date where given, and any use restrictions shown by the repository.
